items.title: Delhi High Court directs takedown of obscene content on Janhvi Kapoor but refuses to ban fan pages
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Tuesday directed the takedown of obscene pornographic online content concerning actor Janhvi Kapoor. Justice Anup Jairam Bhambhani has passed the interim order in a suit filed by Kapoor seeking protection of her personality rights. The Court observed that the submissions made in the plaint and the prayers sought are overbroad. It thus directed Kapoor's counsel to revert with a tabulated chart of the webpages that contain "ex facie pornographic, obscene, prurient, lascivious" content seen to be directly monetising her personality rights to promote sale of merchandise or services. "I am inclined to give you relief in these categories," the Court stated. Anup Jairam Bhambhani Kapoor moved the Court seeking removal of over 5,000 webpages, social media posts containing pornographic AI generated content, impersonating accounts, fake booking agencies and chatbots purportedly commercial exploiting her personality traits without consent. The Court expressed its unwillingness to direct removal of fan pages. "We are not the conscience keepers of the nation. Solution may be worse than the problem. It was at the very root of free speech. You may not be misusing restraint

items.title: Circulating WhatsApp message of COVID cases in locality not offence under Section 505 IPC: J&K High Court
items.summary: The Jammu and Kashmir High Court recently quashed a six-year-old criminal case registered against a man for allegedly circulating a WhatsApp message in 2020 claiming that two COVID-19 positive cases had been detected at a locality in Jammu [ Sandeep Kumar Bhat V/s UT of J&K ]. Justice MA Chowdhary observed that the creation of panic or fear by such an act, by itself, does not satisfy the ingredients of the offence under Section 505(2) of the Indian Penal Code (IPC). "The allegation against the petitioner is only that he circulated a message regarding detection of two Covid-19 positive cases in a particular locality, which allegedly created panic. There is no allegation that the message was intended to create, or was likely to create, feelings of enmity, hatred or ill-will between any two groups based on religion, caste, community, language or any other ground contemplated under Section 505(2) IPC. The creation of panic or fear, by itself, does not satisfy the ingredients of the offence under Section 505(2) IPC," the Court said. Justice M. A. Chowdhary The case concerned one Sandeep Kumar Bhat. items.title: Dhruv Rathee video on Hindu deities eating meat withheld in India after Centre's order: Google tells Delhi HC
items.summary: The Delhi High Court was informed on Tuesday that Dhruv Rathee's YouTube video - in which he allegedly said that Hindu gods Ram, Seeta and Krishna consumed meat and alcohol - has been withheld in India. Google's counsel told Justice Swarana Kanta Sharma that the step was taken after the government's Grievance Appellate Committee (GAC) passed the order. A GAC is a government-established body that allows users to appeal decisions made by social media platforms and other online intermediaries regarding complaints about online content or accounts. The GAC order came after Justice Sharma asked the government to decide Advocate Amita Sachdeva's plea flagging the content in 15 days. Justice Swarana Kanta Sharma Sachdeva today told the Court that the video can still be viewed outside India and in the country using a VPN. She then asked for an order to remove the video globally. However, Google's counsel said that the issue of global removal of content is pending before the Division Bench of the High Court. Sachdeva also told the Bench that some other YouTubers have also uploaded Rathee's video and asked for permission to approach Google with those videos so that they can also be removed. G

items.title: Delhi High Court denies bail to wrestler Sushil Kumar in Sagar Dhankar murder case
items.summary: The Delhi High Court recently denied bail to two-time Olympic medallist Sushil Kumar in wrestler Sagar Dhankar's murder case. Justice Purushaindra Kumar Kaurav said that it was a case of "a premeditated and gruesome assault resulting in death" and that a lot of material is yet to be tested at trial. The Court noted that the Supreme Court had raised concerns over Kumar's conduct before his arrest and that "his capacity to influence the outcome of the trial given his standing, have not been shown to have altered in any material particular". "In these circumstances, this Court is not persuaded that the petitioner has made out a case either for a genuine change in circumstances within the meaning of the liberty reserved by the Supreme Court, or, independently, for the grant of regular bail on the ordinary parameters governing Section 439 CrPC/ 483 BNSS. The application is, accordingly, dismissed," Justice Kaurav ordered. Justice Purushaindra Kumar Kaurav Kumar was denied bail by the trial court on February 6, 2026, in connection with the 2021 murder of junior wrestler Dhankar. items.title: Bike taxis pose safety risks, lack adequate insurance cover: Karnataka tells Supreme Court
items.summary: Motorcycles lack essential passenger-safety features and their use as bike taxis raises concerns over accident vulnerability, insurance coverage and women’s safety, the Karnataka government has told the Supreme Court. The State has challenged a January 23 judgment of the Karnataka High Court, which effectively lifted a court-ordered ban on the operation of bike taxis in Karnataka. A single judge of the Court had earlier ordered that bike taxi services be halted until the State comes out with a policy permitting the same. This ruling was challenged in appeals filed by Ola, Uber, Rapido, motorcycle owners and the Bike Taxi Welfare Association. By the January 2026 judgment, the High Court's Division Bench directed the authorities to consider applications for registering motorcycles as transport vehicles and granting permits to operate them as bike taxis. This ruling has now been challenged by the State before the Supreme Court. In its special leave petition, Karnataka has argued that the High Court effectively converted the discretionary power of transport authorities to grant permits into a mandatory obligation. The State said that motorcycles cannot be permitted to carry passengers

items.title: Anti-abortion rally in Chennai by Catholic groups | LME Shorts
items.summary: Tamil Nadu Assembly Speaker JCD Prabhakar recently spoke at a pro-life event in Chennai, saying, “Life begins at conception” and calling for protection of the “unborn child”. But what if a woman does not want to continue the pregnancy? India’s abortion laws have come a long way — from criminalising abortion under the colonial-era Indian Penal Code to recognising reproductive autonomy as part of the constitutional right to life and personal liberty. So where does Prabhakar’s personal belief end and his public responsibility begin? And what does “supporting women” actually mean if their choice is taken away? Our latest LME Shorts looks at the history of abortion rights in India and the questions raised by the TN Speaker’s pro-life position.
